what: float64 value-and-gradient (and 100-step Adam) programs for mean-square high-order operator residuals of one-hidden-layer tanh ridge networks; candidate = hand-written reverse rule with rematerialised features; controls = autodiff of the closed form, Riccati and JAX Taylor-mode engines in two structures, and the released Laplacian-power compiler.
hardware: one NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB (exclusive), JAX 0.10.2 with jaxlib 0.10.2 CUDA 12 plugins, CPython 3.12

protocol.repetitions: 3 fresh processes (paired by repetition, rotating method order)
protocol.statistic: ratio = strongest-control median / candidate median; lower95 = exp(mean(log r) - 2.920 sd(log r)/sqrt(3))
protocol.qualification: float64; gradients vs 40-digit mpmath on a row subset at atol 1e-8 / rtol 2e-9 (values 1e-9 / 2e-10) for every compared method; full-size outputs finite and digest-compared against the strongest control
protocol.promotion_rule: lower95 >= 1 against every applicable control; >= 2 would be a significant speedup (no row reaches it)

roles.primary: benchmark implementation of the program, counted once per cell in the documented aggregates
roles.package_check: the shipped experimental module measured in the same rotation as its replicate
roles.package_check_replicate: the benchmark implementation repeated beside the shipped module; a replicate, not an extra cell
